about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Gnocchi alla Romana (Baked Semolina Gnocchi)
recipes.summary: Discs of set semolina and milk baked with butter and parmesan until golden and crisp at the edges.
steps: Heat the milk with 1 tsp salt and the nutmeg until steaming. Rain in the semolina, whisking, and stir over low heat for 8 minutes, until very thick.
Off the heat, beat in the yolks and half the cheese. Spread 1.5cm thick on a tray and chill for 30 minutes, until firm.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut into 5cm rounds and overlap in a buttered dish.
Dot with the butter, scatter with the remaining cheese and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Strangolapreti (Trentino Spinach and Bread Dumplings)
recipes.summary: Soft spinach and bread dumplings from Trentino, served with sage butter and parmesan.
steps: Squeeze the spinach very dry and chop finely. Soak the bread in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze lightly.
Mix the bread, spinach, eggs, flour, half the cheese, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Rest for 10 minutes, then shape into 16 oval dumplings.
Simmer in salted water for 8 minutes, until they float and are firm.
Melt the butter with the sage for 2 minutes. Spoon over the dumplings and top with the remaining cheese.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Canederli (Tyrolean Speck and Bread Dumplings)
recipes.summary: Big bread dumplings with ham and parsley from the South Tyrol, tossed in sage butter.
steps: Soften the onion in half the butter for 5 minutes. Soak the bread in the warm milk for 10 minutes.
Mix with the eggs, ham, parsley, flour, salt and pepper. Rest for 10 minutes, then roll into 8 balls with wet hands.
Simmer in salted water for 15 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Melt the remaining butter with the sage and spoon over the dumplings.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Pesce all'Acqua Pazza (Neapolitan Fish in Crazy Water)
recipes.summary: White fish poached in a light broth of cherry tomatoes, garlic and parsley, served with crusty bread.
steps: Cook the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and wine and simmer for 6 minutes, until the tomatoes collapse.
Add the water and salt, then lay in the fish.
Cover and poach gently for 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the broth and toasted bread.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Branzino al Forno (Roast Fish Traybake with Potato and Olives)
recipes.summary: Fish fillets roasted over lemony potatoes, cherry tomatoes and olives on one tray.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with 2 tbsp oil, salt and rosemary on a tray and roast for 25 minutes, until golden.
Add the tomatoes, olives and lemon slices.
Rub the fish with the last of the oil, season and set on top. Roast for 10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Mozzarella in Carrozza (Fried Mozzarella Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Crisp egg-dipped sandwiches with a molten mozzarella centre, a Neapolitan lunch.
steps: Make 4 sandwiches with the bread and mozzarella. Trim the crusts and press the edges firmly.
Whisk the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt. Dust the sandwiches in flour, then soak briefly in the egg.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Cordero Asado (Castilian Roast Lamb with Potatoes)
recipes.summary: Lamb shoulder roasted slowly with garlic and white wine over potatoes until it pulls apart.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Rub the lamb with 1 tbsp oil, paprika, salt and pepper.
Spread the potato, garlic and rosemary in a deep tin with the wine, and rest the lamb on top. Cover with foil.
Roast for 2 1/2 hours, then uncover, drizzle the potato with the remaining oil and roast for 30 minutes, until golden.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes, then pull apart and serve with the potato and pan juices.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Arroz de Marisco (Portuguese Seafood Rice)
recipes.summary: A wet, tomato-rich rice with prawns and white fish, sloppy rather than dry.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes and wine and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover and simmer for 14 minutes.
Fold in the fish and prawns, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until opaque and the rice is soft but still soupy.
Stir in the coriander and rest for 3 minutes.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Espetada (Madeiran Beef Skewers with Garlic and Bay)
recipes.summary: Garlicky beef cubes threaded on bay branches or skewers, grilled and served with bread.
steps: Toss the beef with the garlic, oil, vinegar and salt. Thread onto 4 skewers with the bay leaves.
Grill or barbecue on high for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked to your liking.
Slide the beef off the skewers into the rolls, or serve alongside, with the juices spooned over.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Whole beef cubes are safe once browned outside; cook to at least 70°C if serving well done.

recipes.title: Scouse (Liverpool Lamb and Potato Stew)
recipes.summary: A thick, peppery lamb and root vegetable stew from Liverpool, traditionally served with beetroot or pickles.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the stock, Worcestershire and bay. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potato and simmer for 40 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the potatoes are breaking down.
Season with plenty of pepper.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Schweinebraten (Bavarian Roast Pork with Beer Gravy)
recipes.summary: Crackling-topped pork shoulder roasted over beer and vegetables, with potatoes and a dark gravy.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the pork with 2 tsp salt and the caraway. Set on the onion, carrot and garlic in a tin with the beer.
Roast for 30 minutes, then drop to 160°C (140°C fan) and roast for 1 1/2 hours, adding the potatoes in the last hour.
Rest the pork for 15 minutes. Strain the pan juices, whisk in the flour over heat and simmer for 5 minutes into a gravy.
Slice and serve with the potatoes and gravy.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten from the beer.

recipes.title: Paprikas Krumpli (Hungarian Paprika Potatoes with Sausage)
recipes.summary: A one-pot stew of potatoes, smoked sausage and sweet paprika, a classic comfort dinner.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the paprika so it does not burn.
Add the sausage, tomato and capsicum and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the potato and water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the liquid is thick and red.
notes: Food safety: smoked sausage should be steaming hot throughout, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Segedinsky Gulas (Slovak Pork and Sauerkraut Goulash)
recipes.summary: Pork braised with sauerkraut, paprika and caraway, finished with a swirl of sour cream.
steps: Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes, then stir in the paprika.
Add the sauerkraut, caraway and water. Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream and stir into the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes, until thickened.
Serve with the boiled potatoes.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

recipes.title: Svickova na Smetane (Czech Beef in Creamy Vegetable Sauce)
recipes.summary: Pot-roasted beef sliced and served in a smooth root vegetable and cream sauce.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the carrot, onion, bay and stock, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, turning once, until tender.
Lift out the beef and keep warm. Remove the bay and blend the vegetables and liquid until smooth.
Whisk the flour into the cream and stir into the sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes, then add the lemon juice and season.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce and bread.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Smazeny Syr (Czech Fried Cheese Sandwich)
recipes.summary: A crumbed slab of cheese fried until molten, tucked into a bun with pickles.
steps: Dust the cheese in flour, dip in the beaten egg, then press in breadcrumbs. Repeat the egg and crumbs for a thicker crust and chill for 10 minutes.
Fry in the hot oil for 2 minutes each side, until deep golden. Drain.
Split the rolls and fill with the cheese and pickles.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Cevapi (Bosnian Grilled Beef and Lamb Fingers)
recipes.summary: Small skinless sausages of beef and lamb, grilled and tucked into warm flatbread with raw onion.
steps: Mix the mince, garlic, soda, paprika and 1 1/2 tsp salt well for 3 minutes. Shape into 20 short fingers.
Grill or pan fry for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the pita, fill with the cevapi and top with the onion.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

recipes.title: Pljeskavica (Serbian Spiced Beef and Pork Patty)
recipes.summary: A large, juicy grilled patty served in a bun with onion and tomato.
steps: Mix the mince, grated onion, garlic, soda, 1 1/2 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 4 flat patties 1.5cm thick.
Grill or pan fry for 6 minutes each side, until browned and cooked through.
Fill the buns with the patties, tomato and red onion.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

recipes.title: Sarma (Balkan Cabbage Rolls with Mince and Rice)
recipes.summary: Cabbage leaves wrapped around paprika-spiced beef, pork and rice, simmered in tomato.
steps: Core the cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes. Peel off 12 soft leaves and trim the ribs.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Mix with the mince, rice, paprika, salt and pepper.
Put 3 tbsp on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up. Pack seam-down in a pot.
Pour over the passata and water, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the rice and meat are cooked through.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Burek (Bosnian Meat Pie with Filo)
recipes.summary: Coiled filo pie filled with spiced beef and onion, baked until crisp and golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the onion and mince in 1 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, with salt and pepper, until cooked through. Cool.
Lay 2 filo sheets, brush with oil, spoon the mince along one long edge and roll up. Coil into a greased 26cm tin. Repeat to fill.
Whisk the egg, water and remaining oil and pour over. Bake for 35 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Mici (Romanian Garlic Beef and Pork Rolls)
recipes.summary: Garlic and thyme scented skinless sausages, grilled until charred and served with mustard and bread.
steps: Mix the mince, garlic, soda, paprika, thyme, 1 1/2 tsp salt and pepper, adding the stock slowly. Knead for 3 minutes.
Shape into 12 short rolls and chill for 10 minutes.
Grill or pan fry for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with the rolls and mustard.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork and gluten.

recipes.title: Chiftele (Romanian Herb Meatballs with Mash)
recipes.summary: Fried pork and beef meatballs flavoured with dill and parsley, served over creamy mash.
steps: Mix the mince, onion, egg, crumbs, herbs, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into 16 balls and roll in the flour.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender. Drain and mash with the milk.
Shallow fry the meatballs in the oil for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Serve over the mash with the pan juices spooned on top and extra dill.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Kotlet Mielony (Polish Pork Patties)
recipes.summary: Soft pork patties bound with soaked bread and marjoram, fried until golden and served with potatoes.
steps: Squeeze the roll and mash into the pork with the onion, egg, marjoram, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 patties and coat in crumbs.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender. Drain and toss with the butter.
Fry the patties in the oil for 5 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve the patties with the potatoes and spoon any pan juices over.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Pork mince is safe at 75°C.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Kaldomar (Swedish Cabbage Rolls with Lingonberry)
recipes.summary: Cabbage rolls of pork and beef mince glazed with syrup and butter, served with lingonberry jam.
steps: Blanch the cabbage leaves in boiling water for 3 minutes and trim the ribs. Mix the mince, rice, milk, 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Put 1/8 of the filling on each leaf and roll up. Set seam-down in a buttered dish.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Brush the rolls with syrup, dot with butter and pour in the stock.
Bake for 50 minutes, basting twice, until glazed and cooked through. Serve with the jam.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork and milk.

recipes.title: Kjottkaker (Norwegian Meat Cakes with Brown Gravy)
recipes.summary: Tender beef patties in a brown gravy with boiled potatoes, a Norwegian Sunday staple.
steps: Mix the mince, onion, egg, 1/4 cup flour, milk, nutmeg, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 oval cakes.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender.
Brown the cakes in the butter for 4 minutes each side. Lift out.
Whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the pan, then the stock, and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the cakes and simmer for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Serve with the potato.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Fiskeboller (Norwegian Fish Balls in White Sauce)
recipes.summary: Light, springy white fish balls poached and served in a creamy white sauce with potatoes.
steps: Blend the fish with the egg, cornflour, nutmeg and 1 tsp salt. Add 1 cup milk slowly until smooth. Chill for 15 minutes.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes. Shape the fish mix into 16 balls with wet spoons and poach in simmering salted water for 8 minutes, until firm and white.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and whisk in 1 cup milk. Simmer for 4 minutes until thick.
Serve the balls with the sauce and potatoes.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
